findings.evidence: Line 82: `rcases v with _ | v <;> rcases w with _ | w <;> simp_all <;> split_ifs <;> simp`. The `split_ifs` step needs an `ite` to still be present after `simp_all`.
findings.fix: Use one robust closer instead of the chain, e.g. `rcases v with _ | v <;> rcases w with _ | w <;> simp_all [apply_ite]` or `... <;> simp_all [ite_le_zero]`-style. Or rewrite with the named entry lemmas first, e.g. `· simp only [adjoinPendant_none_some]; split_ifs <;> simp` per case, and finish with `exact hM v w (by simpa using hvw)`.
findings.issue: `simp_all <;> split_ifs <;> simp` only works while `simp_all` leaves the `if j = i then -1 else 0` term untouched in the mixed `none`/`some` cases. If simp's lemma set ever normalizes that term, `split_ifs` errors with no `if` to split. `simp_all` also does three jobs at once (closing `none ≠ none`, rewriting with the entry lemmas, and applying `hM` with the side condition taken from `hvw`), so the reason the proof works is hidden.

findings.evidence: Lines 48–49: the body of `TauCeti.adjoinPendant` is deliberately left unexposed. Lines 50–62 contain the `@[simp]` entry lemmas.
findings.fix: Close the entry goals with the entry lemmas: `ext (_ | v) (_ | w) <;> simp`.
findings.issue: `ext (_ | v) (_ | w) <;> rfl` relies on unfolding `adjoinPendant`, `Matrix.of` and `Matrix.transpose`. The file's own comment (lines 48–49) says the body is deliberately left unexposed, and the entry lemmas `adjoinPendant_none_none`, `adjoinPendant_none_some`, `adjoinPendant_some_none` and `adjoinPendant_some_some` already state these equations.

summary: The new one-line proof of `adjoinPendant_apply_le_zero_of_ne` works only while `simp_all` leaves the `if` term in place, and `adjoinPendant_transpose` still relies on unfolding the definition even though the file says its body is kept unexposed.
